title: The Sleepwalkers
author: Christopher Clark
description: Historian Christopher Clark’s account of how Europe went to war in 1914. It opens with the plot hatched in Belgrade and the murders on the Sarajevo riverbank, and asks why no one stopped what followed.

title: People of the Book
author: Geraldine Brooks
place: National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: A novel that follows a book conservator restoring the Sarajevo Haggadah in 1996, and goes back through the centuries to imagine the people who made, hid, and saved it.

title: Zlata’s Diary
author: Zlata Filipović
description: The diary of a Sarajevo girl who was 11 when the war began, written in the family apartment and the cellar as the shelling went on. It was published during the siege, and her family was flown out in 1993.

title: Logavina Street
author: Barbara Demick
description: American journalist Barbara Demick’s account of the families on one Sarajevo street during the siege: Muslims, Serbs, and Croats living together while the city was shelled.

title: The Cellist of Sarajevo
author: Steven Galloway
description: A novel set during the siege. After a shell kills 22 people waiting in line for bread, a cellist plays for 22 days at the spot. It is based on Vedran Smailović, who played in the ruins after the real attack in 1992.

title: The Fixer
author: Joe Sacco
description: Joe Sacco’s comics reporting on Neven, a Sarajevan who worked as a fixer for foreign journalists, finding them stories and contacts. It is a portrait of the war through one complicated man.
